newsitem.title: ALBANIA: New Albanian parliament to meet on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: New Albanian parliament to meet on Wednesday.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha on Monday issued a decree convening the first session of a new parliament for Wednesday, but his Democratic Party said it would not attend.
Berisha has repeatedly said he will resign once the new parliament is in place but the presidency statement gave no indication of when he planned to step down.
Berisha's Socialist opponents, who won a big majority in the June 29 elections, warned on Sunday that if he failed to issue the decree, they would call the first session themselves.
His own defeated Democrats said they would boycott the session to protest at the conduct of the polls.

"The elections of June 29 were held in a climate of violence and terror exercised by Socialist gangs against supporters of the Democratic Party and the population in general," said a statement issued after a meeting of the party's National Council on Sunday.

It complained that the Democrats had been unable to campaign in the south for the elections, which were described by monitors from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe as acceptable, if far from perfect.
Diplomats say the Democrats' losses even in Tirana and former strongholds such as Kavaje put paid to any serious claims of manipulation.
Berisha's Socialist party opponents and their coalition allies won a total of 117 seats to the Democrats' 27.
Berisha says he has no wish to cohabit with a Socialist government and will resign once he has "fulfilled his constitutional obligations".
His resignation is eagerly awaited by the leftist alliance which fears he will try to influence the makeup of the new cabinet.

Berisha met leaders of his Democrats and smaller parties on Saturday to discuss when parliament should meet and who should be prime minister, but Socialist leaders refused to meet him, saying he no longer had a mandate to decide on the future government.
The president has indicated that he would prefer interim prime minister Bashkim Fino to stay on as premier rather than Socialist leader Fatos Nano, the party's preferred candidate.
Much of the country is still ruled by armed gangs and most Albanians are eager to see a new government take charge and start restoring law and order.
Greece closed its main border crossing into Albania overnight. Greek officials said they had information that armed Albanians would try to abduct a customs officer.

"Traffic between the two countries is now open again, although a bit reduced, and checks are more thorough," a customs officer said. The border has increasingly been closed overnight since the recent political upheaval.
